summary.text: The ozone layer is a region of Earth's stratosphere, mostly about 15 to 35 km up, that absorbs most of the Sun's ultraviolet radiation.
It takes in 97 to 99 percent of the Sun's medium-frequency ultraviolet light, which would otherwise potentially damage exposed life near the surface.
In 1985 research showed industrial chemicals, mainly CFCs, were depleting it, which led to bans, and depletion now appears to have slowed or stopped.

facts.label: Discovered
facts.value: 1913, by Charles Fabry and Henri Buisson

facts.label: Peak concentration
facts.value: 8 to 15 parts per million of ozone

facts.label: Unit of measure
facts.value: The Dobson unit, named after G. Dobson

facts.label: Elsewhere
facts.value: Venus has a thin one, 100 km up

items.prompt: At its densest, how much of the air in the ozone layer is actually ozone?

options.label: About 8 to 15 parts per million
Roughly half of all the air
About one fifth of the air
Close to 5 percent of the air

items.explain: Even at its peak the layer holds only 8 to 15 parts per million of ozone, small compared with other gases in the stratosphere.

items.prompt: Before anyone could fly up and sample it, how did scientists work out that something high in the air was absorbing sunlight?

options.label: Clouds looked darker at certain heights
Weather balloons kept warming as they rose
The sky's blue color slowly faded at noon
Ground sunlight lacked its shortest UV wavelengths

items.explain: Sunlight at the ground matched the expected spectrum except that radiation below about 310 nm was missing, so something in the atmosphere had to be absorbing it.

items.prompt: Why did countries move to ban chlorofluorocarbons?

options.label: They were found to be highly explosive
They were making city smog much worse
They were thinning Earth's UV shield
They were too costly to keep producing

items.explain: Research showed these industrial chemicals were depleting the ozone layer, and fears about the extra ultraviolet radiation led to bans.

items.prompt: If the ozone layer grew much thinner, which human health problem would experts expect to rise?

options.label: Asthma attacks
Skin cancer
Heart disease
Food allergies

items.explain: Ozone depletion lets in more ultraviolet radiation, and increased skin cancer in humans was one of the main concerns.

items.prompt: A weather report gives a reading in Dobson units. What is it describing?

options.label: How strong the wind is aloft
How humid the air is overhead
How bright the sunlight is
How much ozone is overhead

items.explain: The Dobson unit is a convenient measure of the amount of ozone overhead, named after G. Dobson.

items.prompt: Where in the atmosphere would you mainly find the ozone layer?

options.label: Right at ground level
In the upper thermosphere
In the lower stratosphere
At the top of the mesosphere

items.explain: It is mainly found in the lower portion of the stratosphere, roughly 15 to 35 km above Earth.
